title: 50 Most Asked API Interview Questions
summary: A fundamentals-to-advanced bank of 50 backend/SDE API interview questions covering REST and HTTP, methods and status codes, JWT and OAuth 2.0, CORS and security, pagination, rate limiting, caching, API gateways, webhooks, idempotency, versioning, uploads, testing, monitoring, scalability and real-world design scenarios.

chapters.title: API Interview Q&A: What's Inside
points: 50 questions, 10 themed pages of 5, ordered from fundamentals to design scenarios
Page 1: REST and HTTP fundamentals
Page 2: HTTP methods and status codes
Page 3: JWT and session authentication
Page 4: OAuth 2.0 and authorization
Page 5: CORS and API security
Page 6: Pagination, filtering and rate limiting
Page 7: Caching and API gateways
Page 8: Webhooks, idempotency and versioning
Page 9: File uploads, testing and monitoring
Page 10: Scalability and real-world design scenarios
Each answer: one-line short answer, key points and a diagram, table or snippet

chapters.title: REST and HTTP Fundamentals
points: What is a REST API and what are its constraints?
What is the difference between REST, GraphQL and gRPC?
What is the difference between HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3?
What are the main parts of an HTTP request and response?
What does it mean for an API to be stateless, and why does it matter?

chapters.title: HTTP Methods and Status Codes
points: What is the difference between GET and POST?
What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
Which HTTP methods are safe and which are idempotent?
What is the difference between 401 and 403?
When do you return 200, 201, 204, 400, 404, 409, 422 and 5xx?

chapters.title: JWT and Session Authentication
points: How does a JWT work and what are its three parts?
What is the difference between session-based and token-based authentication?
Where should you store a JWT on the client: localStorage or a cookie?
What is the difference between access tokens and refresh tokens?
How do you revoke or invalidate a JWT before it expires?

chapters.title: OAuth 2.0 and Authorization
points: What is OAuth 2.0 and what problem does it solve?
What is the difference between authentication and authorization, and between OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect?
Which OAuth 2.0 grant types exist and when do you use each?
How does the Authorization Code flow with PKCE work?
What is the difference between API keys, Basic auth and Bearer tokens?

chapters.title: CORS and API Security
points: What is CORS and why does the browser enforce it?
What is a preflight request and when is it sent?
What is the difference between CSRF and XSS, and how do you prevent each?
How do you protect an API against OWASP API Top 10 risks like BOLA and injection?
How do you secure an API in transit and at rest?

chapters.title: Pagination, Filtering and Rate Limiting
points: What is the difference between offset and cursor pagination?
How do you design filtering, sorting and field selection in a REST API?
What is rate limiting and why is it needed?
How do the token bucket, leaky bucket and sliding window algorithms differ?
What should a 429 response contain and how should clients handle it?

chapters.title: Caching and API Gateways
points: How does HTTP caching work with Cache-Control, ETag and Last-Modified?
What is the difference between client-side, CDN and server-side caching?
What is cache invalidation and which strategies exist: cache-aside, write-through, write-back?
What is an API gateway and what does it do?
What is the difference between an API gateway, a load balancer and a reverse proxy?

chapters.title: Webhooks, Idempotency and Versioning
points: What is a webhook and how does it differ from polling?
How do you make webhook delivery reliable and secure?
How do you make a POST request idempotent?
What are the API versioning strategies and their trade-offs?
How do you deprecate an API version without breaking clients?

chapters.title: File Uploads, Testing and Monitoring
points: How do you handle large file uploads in an API?
What is the difference between multipart/form-data uploads and direct-to-storage presigned URL uploads?
What is the difference between unit, integration and contract tests for APIs?
What are the key metrics to monitor for an API: RED and the four golden signals?
What is the difference between logging, metrics and distributed tracing?

chapters.title: Scalability and Real-World Design Scenarios
points: How do you scale an API horizontally to handle 10x traffic?
How do you handle a slow or failing downstream dependency with timeouts, retries and a circuit breaker?
What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous APIs, and when do you return 202 Accepted?
How would you design a URL shortener API?
How would you design a payment API that must never double-charge?

chapters.title: API Interview Cheatsheet
points: Method table: safe and idempotent flags for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
Status code quick map: 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx with the ones interviewers probe
401 means unauthenticated, 403 means forbidden, 404 hides resources, 409 conflict, 429 throttled
Auth cheat: JWT structure, short-lived access token plus rotating refresh token, PKCE for public clients
CORS checklist: allowed origins, preflight headers, credentials rules
Pagination pick: offset for small admin lists, cursor for feeds and large data
Rate limit algorithms in one line each: token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window
Caching headers: Cache-Control, ETag with If-None-Match returning 304
Reliability checklist: Idempotency-Key, timeouts, retries with backoff and jitter, circuit breaker
Design answer template: requirements, API contract, data model, scale, failure handling, trade-offs
